definition: Simple random sampling is a sampling method used as a basic comparison point for other designs, described here as requiring the least time and cost. In this context, it is a standard way of selecting a sample for estimating population characteristics.

reasons: The packet supports that simple random sampling uses the least money and time, but it does not support describing it as a “basic comparison point” or a “standard way” of selecting a sample.
The definition adds an unsupported generalization about its role in estimating population characteristics beyond what is stated in the source packet.
The packet does not provide a definition of “simple random sampling”; it only mentions it as a comparison baseline in discussing “ranked set sampling.”

The claim that simple random sampling is “described here as requiring the least time and cost” is not supported by the packet; the packet says ranked set sampling is modified to be more efficient/cost-effective and contrasts it with stratified ranked set sampling and simple random sampling, but it does not state that simple random sampling itself requires the least time and cost.
The claim that simple random sampling is “a standard way of selecting a sample for estimating population characteristics” is not supported anywhere in the packet text provided.
